summary: Over 14 days the AAPS closed loop maintained an overall time-in-range of 86.0% with average glucose 121.6 mg/dL, alongside three severe hypoglycemia clusters and two severe hyperglycemia clusters, plus one unresolved high-IOB event at the very end of the window. Telemetry and profile completeness are strong, but zero carbohydrate entries were logged in the entire period, which blocks direct separation of meal, basal, correction, and IOB effects for several recurring patterns. The active aaps_profile is treated as authoritative and applicable across the full period per profile_context, despite a mid-period profile switch on 2026-08-13. Dynamic ISF is actively compensating during high-deviation events, autosens is appropriately disabled to avoid overlap, and neither the max basal nor max IOB ceiling was a limiting or runaway factor. The most consistent safety-relevant signal is repeated glucose decline continuing 4-6 hours after correction boluses, coinciding at least once with an unusually large UAM boost multiplier, which competes with a long declared DIA (10 hours) as an explanation. A second unresolved pattern is recurring midday and afternoon hyperglycemia in hours where basal is comparatively low, which competes with a plausible but unconfirmed unannounced-meal explanation due to the total absence of carb data. No profile or AAPS parameter change is strongly enough supported to recommend now; the priority is safe, sequential verification.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage was 98.7% with 5-minute cadence, 0 invalid or duplicate entries, and 10 gaps (max 65 minutes). Insulin and device-status telemetry were extensive (655 insulin entries, 6214 device statuses). Carbohydrate entries were zero for the entire 14-day window. A profile switch to a diluted U200 flat-ISF strategy occurred mid-period (2026-08-13 21:23); profile_context declares the current aaps_profile historically applicable to the whole period, so pre- and post-switch data are both used, with slightly lower weight given to the first and last partial days (33 and 269 entries).
analysis_steps.evidence: telemetry.data_quality fields; telemetry.metadata.counts; representative_events Profile Switch entries; profile_context.historical_applicability=yes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero carbohydrate treatment entries for the full period; no pre-switch profile snapshot to independently cross-check early-period behavior.

analysis_steps.findings: Time below range was 5.1% and time above range 8.9%, with several days showing simultaneous elevated TAR and TBR (overcorrection-swing signature) rather than pure basal mistiming. Severe hypoglycemia clusters occurred on 2026-08-13 (down to 42 mg/dL), 2026-08-14 (down to 41 mg/dL), and 2026-08-21 (42 mg/dL); severe hyperglycemia clusters occurred on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18 (up to 293 and 290 mg/dL). The final loop status of the period (2026-08-21 21:09) shows an unresolved escalation with IOB 5.935 U and glucose 245 mg/dL, with outcome outside the data window. Confounders present in the period include an occlusion and pump error announcement (2026-08-19), several site and sensor changes, and GLP-1 dosing notes that can alter absorption and gastric emptying independent of profile settings.
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_summary; glucose_extremes list; representative_loop_statuses final entry; representative_events (Site Change, Sensor Change, Announcement, GLP-1 notes).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No confirmation of the outcome following the final unresolved high-IOB event beyond the data window.

analysis_steps.findings: Total scheduled basal (~16.2 U/day) is internally consistent with the user's declared dilute-basal strategy. Overnight and early-morning hours show the highest time-below-range of the day despite modest scheduled basal (0.6-0.7 U/h), which is more consistent with lingering bolus IOB than basal excess. The worst hyperglycemia of the day occurs in the 10:00-17:00 local window, coinciding with the lowest basal segment (0.5 U/h at 16:00), which is a plausible but unconfirmed basal-insufficiency signal that competes directly with an unannounced-meal explanation, since no carbohydrate data exists to separate them. Frequent manual temporary targets (135 mg/dL, variable duration) reflect user-driven overrides that must be excluded from baseline profile-behavior conclusions.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local; aaps_profile.basal_segments; representative_events Temporary Target entries.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate timing/amount to separate meal-driven afternoon rises from basal insufficiency.

analysis_steps.findings: ISF is intentionally flat (56 mg/dL/U) with Dynamic ISF doing time-of-day adjustment (dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=70%); observed variable_sens ranged widely (about 27.8-148.8 mg/dL/U), dropping steeply during the largest hyperglycemic/high-IOB events, consistent with the automation compensating for real-time resistance rather than a static-ISF defect. Carb ratio is lowest (10.5 g/U) at 16:00, coinciding with the worst afternoon hyperglycemia, but this cannot be confirmed as CR insufficiency without carb data. Multiple therapy_response_windows show glucose continuing to fall substantially 4-6 hours after correction boluses (for example -173, -176, -132 mg/dL by 360 minutes), which is consistent with a long insulin tail relative to the declared DIA of 10 hours, but this competes with an isolated extreme UAM boost multiplier (35.93) recorded just before one of the same hypoglycemia clusters (2026-08-13), so the delayed-hypoglycemia pattern cannot yet be attributed to DIA alone.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.isf_segments; aaps_profile.carb_ratio_segments; aaps_profile.dia_hours; representative_loop_statuses variable_sens values; therapy_response_windows change_360m_mg_dl values.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate data to isolate CR adequacy; no independent confirmation of actual pharmacodynamic tail beyond loop-derived estimates.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled and functioning as expected for a closed-loop system with COB always at zero (consistent with zero logged carbs); all daytime dosing is deviation-based (UAM), not COB-based, meaning the carbohydrate-absorption subsystem (min_5m_carbimpact, meal_max_absorption_hours) is structurally untested in this data. One UAM Boost 2 value of 35.93 (2026-08-13 13:55) is a marked outlier relative to typical values (0.2-2.0) and occurred shortly before the matching severe hypoglycemia cluster, providing a plausible compounding or alternative explanation to the DIA hypothesis. Checking smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled=false against the recurring 135 mg/dL temporary targets found no direct timing overlap with the severe events, so this remains an unresolved but low-priority uncertainty rather than supporting evidence for a change. SMB interval and basal-minute limits (3/15/20 minutes) show no internal inconsistency.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.smb_settings; representative_loop_statuses reason strings (UAM Boost 2 value); representative_events Temporary Target timestamps; treatment_summary.carb_entries=0.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate data to exercise or validate the COB-based subsystem; UAM Boost 35.93 outlier not independently explained.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is disabled while Dynamic ISF is enabled, a valid non-overlapping configuration; observed sensitivity_ratio values near 1 (0.79-1.0) represent the expected neutral state with autosens off, not a disabled or malfunctioning system. Max basal (12 U/h) and max IOB (25 U) were never approached (peak observed IOB 5.935 U; peak enacted rate about 4 U/h), so neither ceiling was a limiting or runaway-risk factor in this window. However, the effective correction ceiling actually reached during the worst hyperglycemia events consistently matched roughly six times the scheduled basal rate for that local hour (current_basal_safety_multiplier=6.0), directly linking the automation's real-world correction capacity to the same basal segments flagged as a possible insufficiency in basal_targets. This creates a concrete dependency: raising the relevant basal segment and raising the safety multiplier are two non-simultaneous levers for the same effect and must not be adjusted together.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.smb_settings.raw_settings (autosens_enabled, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled, current_basal_safety_multiplier, max_basal_u_per_hour, max_iob_units); representative_loop_statuses enacted/suggested rate values around 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-21.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No data isolating whether the 6x multiplier or the basal segment itself is the more appropriate lever if a change is ever supported.

analysis_steps.findings: The user-declared analysis_context.meal_strategies is an empty list with strategy_stable_for_period null, meaning no prebolus minutes, immediate bolus percentage, or e-carb protocol is declared; this is a genuine absence, not a Nightscout confirmation gap, and is independently corroborated by zero logged carbohydrate treatments. All 40 representative_treatments and 24 therapy_response_windows are Correction Bolus or Temp Basal only. A recurring pattern (8 of 24 windows, late-morning/midday) shows glucose continuing to rise for 120-240 minutes despite a small correction bolus already given, consistent with possible unannounced meals but not confirmed. A second recurring pattern (5 of 24 windows, afternoon/evening) shows outsized or biphasic drops after moderate-to-large corrections, overlapping twice with the severe hypoglycemia clusters and once with the UAM Boost outlier, pointing more toward automation/IOB-stacking behavior than meal-bolus timing.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.analysis_context.meal_strategies; treatment_summary.carb_entries=0; representative_treatments; therapy_response_windows timestamps and change_120m/240m/360m values.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate amount or meal timestamp exists anywhere in the package to confirm or refute the unannounced-meal hypothesis for the late-morning/midday pattern.

analysis_steps.findings: extended_carb_entries is 0 and average_extended_carb_duration_min is null; no e-carb amount, start offset, or duration exists in either the declared strategy or the telemetry. No comparison between e-carbs and observed glucose action time is possible, and none is invented.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete absence of any e-carb or regular-carb record; this stage cannot progress until at least one carb or e-carb entry exists.

analysis_steps.findings: Two competing explanations remain unresolved and must not be collapsed into a single change: (1) repeated glucose decline continuing 4-6 hours after correction boluses, plausibly linked to the declared 10-hour DIA but also plausibly linked to an isolated extreme UAM boost event; and (2) recurring midday/afternoon hyperglycemia in the lowest scheduled basal window, plausibly linked to basal insufficiency but equally plausibly linked to unannounced meals, given zero carbohydrate data across the entire period. The automation layer (Dynamic ISF, SMB/UAM, safety multiplier) is functioning within its own logic and is not itself misconfigured; it is actively compensating for whichever underlying gap exists, which is why severe excursions persist despite visible compensation. The mid-period profile switch (2026-08-13) is treated as fully applicable across the period per profile_context, correcting an earlier over-cautious weighting of pre-switch data. No profile or AAPS parameter has sufficient, unambiguous, single-cause evidence to support a numeric change today; the safest path is sequential verification starting with data collection (carb logging) and clinical review of DIA, before any basal, CR, or multiplier change is considered, and never changing basal and the safety multiplier together.
analysis_steps.evidence: Aggregated findings from data_quality through meal_ecarbs_absorption stages; profile_context.historical_applicability=yes; decision_inventory current values.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: Carbohydrate logging remains the single largest gap limiting resolution of both major competing-explanation pairs.

strengths: CGM data quality is strong (98.7% coverage, 5-minute cadence, no invalid or duplicate entries), supporting confident glucose-pattern analysis.
Overall time-in-range across the 14 days was 86.0%, with several individual days above 90% TIR.
Dynamic ISF and SMB/UAM show clear, appropriate real-time compensation during high-deviation events, with sensitivity values dropping exactly when resistance appears highest.
Autosens and Dynamic ISF are configured without functional overlap (autosens disabled while Dynamic ISF is enabled), avoiding a common double-adjustment error.
Neither the max basal (12 U/h) nor max IOB (25 U) ceiling was approached during the period, indicating no runaway-dosing risk from those specific limits in this window.
Overnight glucose control outside of tail-effect lows was generally stable, with automation correctly reducing or zeroing basal when low guard glucose was predicted.
issues: Three separate severe hypoglycemia clusters (as low as 41-42 mg/dL) occurred on 2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, and 2026-08-21, each following a correction bolus by several hours.
Two severe hyperglycemia clusters (up to 293 and 290 mg/dL) occurred on 2026-08-15 and 2026-08-18.
Several days show simultaneous elevated time-above-range and time-below-range, a pattern more consistent with overcorrection swings than a single simple profile defect.
Zero carbohydrate entries were logged across the entire 14-day period, blocking direct separation of meal effects from basal, CR, and automation effects in multiple recurring patterns.
One UAM boost multiplier (35.93 on 2026-08-13) is a marked outlier relative to all other observed values and occurred shortly before a severe hypoglycemia cluster.
The final recorded loop status of the period (2026-08-21 21:09) shows an unresolved escalation with IOB near 5.9 U and glucose 245 mg/dL, with no visibility into the outcome.

recommendations.title: Clinically verify DIA and correction-bolus tail behavior before any change
recommendations.description: Multiple therapy-response windows show glucose still falling substantially 4-6 hours after a correction bolus, coinciding at least once with an unusually large UAM boost multiplier and twice with severe hypoglycemia clusters. This pattern could reflect the declared 10-hour DIA, an isolated automation event, or both, and these two explanations have not been separated by current data.

suggested_change.proposed_direction: discuss with a diabetes care provider whether the declared DIA correctly matches actual insulin action for the diluted U200 strategy before considering any numeric change, and review the isolated UAM boost event separately

recommendations.title: Begin structured carbohydrate logging to separate meal, basal, and CR effects
recommendations.description: Zero carbohydrate entries exist across the full 14-day period, which blocks confirmation of whether recurring late-morning/midday and afternoon hyperglycemia reflects unannounced meals, insufficient carb ratio, or insufficient basal.

suggested_change.proposed_direction: log carbohydrate amount and timestamp for representative meals, particularly around the late-morning/midday and afternoon hours already flagged as recurring patterns

recommendations.title: Do not adjust afternoon/evening basal segments and the automation safety multiplier at the same time
recommendations.description: The effective correction ceiling reached during hyperglycemia events consistently matched about six times the scheduled basal rate for that hour, linking the automation safety multiplier directly to the 16:00, 18:00, and 19:00 basal segments. Changing both together would make it impossible to attribute any resulting change in outcomes to either lever.

suggested_change.proposed_direction: resolve the meal-vs-basal ambiguity (see carbohydrate logging recommendation) before considering a change to either the basal segments or the safety multiplier, and change at most one of the two if evidence later supports it

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep the current 10-hour DIA setting for now rather than changing it, given that the repeated delayed post-correction glucose decline has at least one competing explanation (an isolated extreme UAM boost event) that has not been ruled out.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Therapy-response windows show substantial glucose decline continuing 4-6 hours after correction boluses on several dates, which is consistent with a long insulin tail relative to DIA, but the same hypoglycemia cluster on 2026-08-13 is also preceded by an unusually large UAM boost multiplier (35.93), so the cause cannot be attributed to DIA alone with current evidence.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Review the timing and magnitude of correction boluses against the 4-6 hour glucose response with a diabetes care provider, and separately examine why the 2026-08-13 UAM boost value was so much larger than typical, before considering any DIA change.

The flat ISF is a deliberate declared strategy with Dynamic ISF performing time-of-day adjustment; observed variable sensitivity compensates appropriately during high-deviation events, showing no isolated defect in the static value itself.

Repeated 4-6 hour delayed glucose decline after correction boluses is consistent with a long insulin tail relative to this DIA, but at least one hypoglycemia cluster is equally explained by an isolated extreme UAM boost event, so the two explanations have not been separated. This is the primary item recommended for clinical verification before any change.

The related current_basal_safety_multiplier creates a dependency with the 16:00-19:00 basal segments and must not be changed together with them.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: The declared meal strategy is currently empty (no prebolus timing, no immediate bolus percentage, and no e-carb protocol), and the observed strategy is fully reactive: all daytime glucose management is handled by UAM/SMB microbolusing and small manual correction boluses, with zero carbohydrates logged in 14 days. Rather than proposing a specific prebolus time, bolus percentage, or e-carb duration that the data does not support, the most useful step is to begin logging real meals so that a prebolus timing and immediate bolus percentage can be evaluated against actual absorption, while SMB/UAM continues to handle unannounced variability as it currently does.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Without any carbohydrate entries, it is not possible to determine whether the recurring late-morning/midday rise pattern reflects an uncovered meal, an insufficient carb ratio, or endogenous glucose rise, nor whether e-carbs would help, since no e-carb or extended-bolus data exists to evaluate action time.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log carbohydrate amount and timestamp for a handful of representative meals during the late-morning/midday hours already flagged as a recurring rise-despite-correction pattern; this single addition would most improve confidence for separating meal, CR, and basal effects.

implementation_steps: Review this analysis with a diabetes care provider before making any changes; do not adjust AAPS settings automatically based on this report.
Begin logging carbohydrate amount and timestamp for representative meals, prioritizing the late-morning/midday hours already flagged as a recurring pattern.

Discuss the repeated 4-6 hour delayed glucose decline after correction boluses and the isolated large UAM boost event with a care provider, specifically to clarify whether the declared 10-hour DIA is appropriate before any change.
After at least one to two weeks of carbohydrate logging, re-run this analysis to re-evaluate whether the afternoon hyperglycemia pattern is better explained by meals, carb ratio, or basal.
If a basal or safety-multiplier change is ever considered afterward, change only one of the two at a time and monitor glucose closely before making a second change.
Continue monitoring for any further extreme automation events (comparable to the 2026-08-13 UAM boost outlier) and note their timing relative to subsequent glucose lows.
education: Dynamic ISF can substantially change the effective insulin sensitivity used for each dosing decision even when the profile's static ISF value stays flat; large swings in this real-time value during high-glucose events are expected behavior, not necessarily a sign of a wrong profile setting.

The automation's maximum deliverable correction rate during a hyperglycemia event can be governed by a safety multiplier applied to the scheduled basal rate for that hour, rather than by the flat maximum basal ceiling; this creates a hidden link between two settings that should not be changed at the same time.

A correction bolus can still be followed by significant glucose movement 4-6 hours later; this delayed effect can reflect either the insulin's duration of action setting or a single unusually large automated dose, and these two causes need to be told apart before changing duration of action.
Days with both elevated time-above-range and elevated time-below-range often indicate overcorrection swings rather than a single simple basal or target problem.

Without logged carbohydrate data, even a very complete CGM and insulin dataset cannot reliably separate meal effects from basal or carb-ratio effects; carbohydrate logging is often the single highest-value addition to future analysis.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only; it does not provide medical advice and does not replace guidance from a qualified diabetes care provider.
The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely after any change.
Do not change AAPS automation or profile settings automatically based on this report; all changes should be discussed with a care team first.

Given the severe hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia events identified in this period, any settings review should prioritize safety verification (particularly around correction-bolus timing and DIA) before considering efficiency-focused changes.
Basal segments and the automation safety multiplier are linked; changing both at the same time would prevent safely attributing any resulting effect to either change.
